An Overview of the 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition         xv
An Overview of the 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition
Arun Chaturvedi
Leader & Station Commander
The 27th Indian Antarctic Expedition was flagged off from V asco,
Goa o n 6th December 2007, by Dr. P.S. Goel, Secretary, Ministry of
Earth Sciences (MoES); in the presence of Dr. Rasik Ravindra, Centre
Director, NCAOR. The expedition team had 61 members; 26 for the Polar
Winter, and 35 for the Polar Summer. It was an all-male expedition-team.
Summary of the Voyage: Some of the members, with longer duration
scientific experiments and logistic tasks, had taken earlier DROMLAN
flights from Cape Town (South Africa) to Antarctica, in November 2007;
the remaining members of the team boarded the ship MV Emerald Sea at
Goa.
The Scientific experiments and logistic tasks were planned in two
distinctly separate regions— first at Indian Antarctic Station Maitri and its
surrounding area; and the other at the new site selected for the third Indian
Antarctic station, on Bharati Island in Larsemann Hills area. Since both
the locations are about 3000 km apart; the work-plan was to finish the
tasks at Maitri, as early as possible, and then to leave the ship for Larsemann
Hills area quickly. The Leader of the Expedition (Arun Chaturvedi) was to
stay back with the Winter team at Maitri; while Shri Ajay Dhar was declared
the V oyage Leader for Larsemann Hills work, and he was to return to India
with the Summer team.
The ship had left Goa, India on 6th December 2007. After almost a
month, it reached the coastal area near India Bay on 3rd January 2008. The
team worked furiously at Maitri between 3 Jan – 14 Feb; and then on 15th
February 2008 the ship left India Bay. After about ten days of sailing, the
ship arrived at Larsemann Hills coast on 24th February 2008 and the team
worked at the new station site on Bharati Island and its surrounding area.
After finishing all the tasks, the ship left Larsemann Hills area on 9th March
and the Summer team reached back Goa on 11th April 2008.
Scientific Objectives: The team had a participation from 19 different
scientific organizations— various Govt. Departments, Research Institutes
and Universities. These were— National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean
Research (NCAOR), Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian Institute
of Geomagnetism (IIG), India Meteorological Department (IMD), National
Physical Laboratory (NPL), National Geophysical Research Institute
xvi                                                   Arun Chaturvedi
(NGRI), Snow and Avalanche Study Establishment (SASE), All India
Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) , Birbal Sahni Institute of
Palaeobotany (BSIP), Survey of India (SOI), Shriram Institute of Industrial
Research (SIIR), Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), National Hydrographic
Office (NHO), Space Physics Laboratory (SPL), Indian Centre for Space
Physics (ICSP), Barkatulla University (BU), Viswa Bharati (VU), Avadh
University (AU), Nicholas Piramal Research Centre (NPRC). All the
organizations, barring the last two, have submitted scientific papers about
the work carried out by them in Antarctica. These papers have been included
in this Report.
It is worth emphasizing that the team got just 42 days’ of summer
time at Maitri; and even within this period, about 13 days were lost to
blizzards and high winds. Thus, within the constraint of just one month’s
working time, the team achieved almost all the scientific objectives, which
is quite creditable.
The summer team at Larsemann Hills got only 14 days of total time
and finished all the listed scientific work satisfactorily; this was
meticulously planned and supervised by Shri Ajay Dhar.
During the wintering period, one major achievement was depth-
profiling of frozen lakes of Schirmacher Oasis by using the GPR. This
work was done during the peak polar winter, by taking PB-vehicle tracked
GPR to extremely difficult areas. Thus Indian scientists have brought out
the first-ever depth-data from even the inaccessible epi-shelf lakes of
Schirmacher Oasis. This work has demonstrated the sub-shelf channel
connection of these lakes to the high tides of the Southern Ocean (Photo-
1).
Logistic Objectives: Apart from the routine logistic necessities of
every Antarctic Expedition, like— shifting of all fuel, supplies, equipment
to Maitri station and back-loading the cargo of the previous team; this
Expedition had four major logistic objectives:
1. Construction of an Earth Station at Maitri, to link Indian Antarctic
Station to India.
2. Construction of a new eco-friendly Toilet & Bath Complex at
Maitri, as desired by the Hon’ble Minister during his Antarctic visit
in February 2005.
3. Preparatory work at Bharati Island, the new Antarctic station
site in Larsemann Hills.
4. Testing a new policy-decision of all Logistic Maintenance and Coastal
